raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes repeated video encoding in chunked prefill. A long video was run through the vision encoder once per chunk, so two or three times per request. Now it is encoded once.

## Motivation

When a prompt is longer than `chunked_prefill_size`, prefill runs in chunks. Each chunk looks for the encoder output in the embedding cache. If it is not there, the chunk runs the encoder again on the whole video, not only on the part it needs.

For a long video it is usually not there:

- The cache is 100 MiB by default. The encoder output of a long video is bigger than that, so it is never stored.
- Qwen3-VL on a Hopper GPU with 60 GiB or more runs with the cache off.
- An entry can be evicted between two chunks of the same request.

So a request with 3 chunks runs the encoder 3 times. A large image or an audio clip that is cut by a chunk boundary has the same problem.

I found this while profiling Qwen3-VL video requests: the vision encoder ran twice for one 16.5 s clip.

## Reproduction

Environment:

- GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB (`chunked_prefill_size` is 8192)
- Base: upstream `58cb1a2be6ab` for the first table (first version of this PR); upstream `abf92826ee` for the EVS table and the checks of this revision
- Server: default arguments. Qwen3.5-27B and the EVS model also get `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`, so the language-model prefill runs eagerly for every model.
- Input: synthetic 1280x720 clips, one video per request, streamed chat completions, 16 output tokens
- A forward hook on the vision encoder (on `mlp1` for the EVS model) counts how many times it runs per request.

| Model | Clip | Video tokens | Encoder output | Prefill chunks | Encoder runs before | Encoder runs after |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct` | 16.5 s | 9,216 | 288 MiB | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B` | 33.5 s | 11,550 | 113 MiB | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct` | 33.5 s | 23,760 | 162 MiB | 3 | 3 | 1 |
| `zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking` | 16.5 s | 20,332 | 159 MiB | 3 | 3 | 1 |

A shorter clip whose output fits the cache is encoded once on the base as well. For example the 16.5 s clip on Qwen3.5-27B has 9,216 tokens and 90 MiB of output, uses 2 chunks, and runs the encoder once.

EVS model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-BF16` with `video_pruning_rate` 0.7 (from its config), a 66 s clip (128 frames), one request at a time. At 0.7 the clip keeps 9,830 rows, 96 MiB, which fits the default 100 MiB cache, so these runs set `SGLANG_VLM_CACHE_SIZE_MB=0` to show the repeated encoding:

| Chunk size | Video tokens | Prefill chunks | Encoder runs before | Encoder runs after | Median TTFT before | Median TTFT after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 (default) | 9,830 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 5,875 ms | 5,411 ms |
| 2048 | 9,830 | 6 | 6 | 1 | 7,654 ms | 5,389 ms |

The TTFT values of this table come from one launch of 4 requests per tree. With the default cache both trees run the encoder once, and the change keeps the cache's own tensor instead of a copy. The server logs show EVS enabled at 0.7 and no warning or error.

A long video also emptied the cache for other requests: `MultiModalStaticCache.set()` evicted every entry before finding that the new one can never fit. `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct`, default 100 MiB cache, one request at a time, `--disable-radix-cache` (otherwise the repeated prompt would reuse its KV and never look at the cache). A 16.5 s clip (11,520 tokens, 79 MiB of encoder output, fits) is sent again after each of 8 different 33.5 s clips (23,760 tokens, 162 MiB, does not fit); 2 launches per tree, on `abf92826ee`:

| Tree | Encoder runs of the repeated 16.5 s clip | Its median TTFT | Median TTFT of the 33.5 s clips |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| this PR without the `set()` check | 16 of 16 requests | 1,098 ms | 2,422 ms |
| this PR | 0 of 16 | 833 ms | 2,420 ms |

## Modifications

- When the first chunk runs the encoder, keep the part of its output that later chunks still need, in a table in `mm_schedule` (`_prefill_rows`). The key is the item's hash and its positions in the prompt.
- Read the kept rows in later chunks before looking at the cache. In `_get_chunked_embedding_full` the cache is asked only when nothing is kept, so later chunks no longer touch its LRU order.
- Drop the part already read, so only the unread part stays in memory.
- Remove an entry after the item's last chunk. The scheduler also empties the table whenever no request is between two prefill chunks: at the start of `get_new_batch_prefill`, in the dLLM branch of `get_next_batch_to_run` while no context prefill is part-way (`DllmManager.any_context_in_progress()`), when a dLLM request is aborted, and in `pause_generation`, `flush_cache` and `release_memory_occupation`.
- Add `MultiModalStaticCache.peek()`, which reads an entry without changing the LRU order.
- `MultiModalStaticCache.set()` refuses an entry larger than the whole cache before evicting anything, so a long video no longer empties the cache for every other request. #42062 makes the same change.
- Check that the kept rows cover the chunk before slicing them.
- Cover the three chunked paths: `_get_chunked_embedding_full`, `_batch_encode_per_image_misses` and `_get_chunked_embedding_by_item`.
- Add unit tests for the three paths, EVS, a cache entry evicted between two chunks, an encoder that reuses its output buffer, a restarted prefill, items shared by session requests, the same image twice in one prompt, every place the scheduler empties the table, and an entry larger than the cache.

No new flag or config. A request that fits in one chunk takes the same path as before. `schedule_batch.py` is not changed, and nothing is stored in `model_specific_data`.

What is kept is a copy of the unread part, not the encoder output itself. The output can be a slice of a larger batch tensor, and keeping the slice would keep the whole batch alive. The copy is made again only after half of it has been read, so a video with many chunks is not copied once per chunk. If the cache holds the same tensor, it is kept by reference and nothing is copied; when `set()` stored a clone of the output, the clone is read and kept instead.

Requests with the same items at the same positions share an entry (session requests, identical prompts). That is safe because the rows depend only on the content, and a request reads an entry only from the position where its unread rows begin. The positions are part of the key because the same image twice in one prompt has the same hash; with the hash alone, the second copy would read rows of the first.

Where the table is emptied: `get_new_batch_prefill` is reached by every prefill loop after an abort, a disagg bootstrap failure or an optimistic yield has dropped the chunked request, and before a new request becomes the chunked one. Outside dLLM only the chunked request keeps rows into the next step, so the table holds the items of one request.

Making the cache bigger with `SGLANG_VLM_CACHE_SIZE_MB` does not fix this. The cache is shared and evicts the least recently used entry, so a request can still lose its entry between two chunks.

A precomputed embedding that is too short now fails at the new check instead of later in `_adjust_embedding_length`.

Not changed here: models that run the encoder inside their own `forward` (the legacy LLaVA family) have the same problem and need a separate change.

## Accuracy Tests

On upstream `abf92826ee` with this PR applied, H100 80GB:

```bash
pytest \
  test/registered/chunked_prefill/test_mm_chunked_embedding_unit.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_multimodal_abort_cleanup.py
```

Result:

```text
73 passed
```

This includes 32 new cases and 41 existing ones. pre-commit passes on the changed files.

The tests under `test/registered/chunked_prefill`, `unit/managers`, `unit/multimodal`, `unit/disaggregation`, `unit/mem_cache`, `unit/hardware_backend` and `unit/dllm` fail in the same places with and without the change on that machine: tests that need four GPUs or a Rust toolchain, the unified HiCache tests, and the two tensor-parallel-rank tests of `test_mm_process_config.py`.

The change does not alter the model output. Greedy decoding, long clips, the 8 generated tokens and the top-5 logprobs of the first 5 tokens, with and without the change:

| Model | Base | Tokens compared | Tokens that differ | Logprob positions compared | Positions that differ |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-VL-8B | `58cb1a2be6ab`, first version | 64 | 0 | 40 | 0 |
| Qwen3.5-27B | `58cb1a2be6ab`, first version | 64 | 0 | 40 | 0 |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B | `58cb1a2be6ab`, first version | 64 | 0 | 40 | 0 |
| GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking | `58cb1a2be6ab`, first version | 64 | 0 | 40 | 0 |
| Qwen3-VL-8B | `abf92826ee`, this revision against the first version | 64 | 0 | 40 | 0 |
| Nemotron Nano 12B v2 VL, EVS, chunk 8192 | `abf92826ee` | 64 | 0 | 40 | 0 |
| Nemotron Nano 12B v2 VL, EVS, chunk 2048 | `abf92826ee` | 64 | 0 | 40 | 0 |

Two launches of the base server also give identical results, so the comparison is exact.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

TTFT, one request at a time, first version of this PR on `58cb1a2be6ab`. Base and patched servers are started in turn, 3 launches each, 10 requests per launch.

| Model | Clip | TTFT before | TTFT after | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-VL-8B | 16.5 s | 764 ms | 640 ms | -16% |
| Qwen3.5-27B | 33.5 s | 2,091 ms | 1,983 ms | -5% |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B | 33.5 s | 3,735 ms | 2,417 ms | -35% |
| GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking | 16.5 s | 2,615 ms | 1,929 ms | -26% |

Shorter clips that were already encoded once did not change (within 14 ms on all four models).

48 requests, sent 4 or 8 at a time, first version on `58cb1a2be6ab`, one server launch per row:

| Model | At once | req/s before | req/s after | Median TTFT before | Median TTFT after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-VL-8B | 4 | 1.49 | 1.79 | 1,945 ms | 1,704 ms |
| Qwen3-VL-8B | 8 | 1.54 | 1.92 | 3,086 ms | 2,588 ms |
| Qwen3.5-27B | 4 | 0.60 | 0.68 | 5,031 ms | 4,495 ms |
| Qwen3.5-27B | 8 | 0.64 | 0.74 | 7,414 ms | 6,463 ms |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B | 4 | 0.28 | 0.57 | 9,753 ms | 5,523 ms |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B | 8 | 0.29 | 0.62 | 16,646 ms | 8,643 ms |
| GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking | 4 | 0.45 | 0.70 | 6,277 ms | 4,248 ms |
| GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking | 8 | 0.46 | 0.75 | 10,627 ms | 6,866 ms |

The same test for this revision on `abf92826ee`, Qwen3-VL-8B, 4 launches per row (mean req/s, median of the per-launch median TTFT):

| At once | Encoder runs per 48 requests, before / after | req/s before | req/s after | Median TTFT before | Median TTFT after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 96 / 48 | 1.48 | 1.76 | 1,942 ms | 1,708 ms |
| 8 | 101-102 / 48 | 1.53 | 1.89 | 3,100 ms | 2,713 ms |

Peak GPU memory (`torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated`, MiB), first version on `58cb1a2be6ab`:

|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-VL-8B | 64,760 / 64,760 | 65,697 / 65,370 |

They are the part of the video after the first chunk, so they grow with the video and are not counted in `SGLANG_VLM_CACHE_SIZE_MB`. With several requests the peak is lower because the repeated encoder runs are gone. This revision on `abf92826ee` gives the same Qwen3-VL-8B peak at 8 at once in all 4 launches (65,697 / 65,371 MiB).

@JustinTong0323 Thanks a lot for the detailed review! I pushed the changes and replied to each comment above.

For the other three points:
- `set()` with an oversize entry: added the size check in e5830d1b59, so an entry that can't fit no longer empties the whole cache. I also checked it on a GPU with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and the default cache: a short clip sent again after long ones was re-encoded every time before (16 of 16) and never after (0 of 16), and its TTFT went from 1,098 to 833 ms.
- EVS: I ran Nemotron Nano 12B v2 VL on an H100. Its pruned output fits in the default cache, so I turned the cache off to reproduce the problem. The encoder ran once per chunk before (2 or 6 times, depending on chunk size) and once after, with identical outputs. Numbers are in the description.
- `flush_cache`: I'll open a separate PR for it.

While re-reading the whole change I also fixed two small things: a dLLM request aborted halfway through its context could leave its kept rows in the table (56b02aff94), and the full path made one extra copy when `set()` stored a clone (0ef58b54be).

Could you add the `run-ci` label when you get a chance? Thanks!

The retention mechanism is the right shape for this bug, and the evidence package (encoder-call counts, logprob-exact parity, peak-memory tables) is thorough. Details in the line comments; three things that don't anchor to this diff:

1. `MultiModalStaticCache.set()` evicts before checking whether the entry can ever fit (`mem_cache/multimodal_cache.py:115-119`): an oversize entry — exactly the long-video case here — flushes the *entire* cache and then returns `False`. Every first chunk of a long video therefore still wipes every other request's cached embeddings under this PR. `if data_size > self.max_size: return False` before the eviction loop fixes it; worth landing here or immediately after, since this workload is the PR's motivation.
2. The EVS path is unit-tested only per the PR description. Please run one EVS model on a GPU before merge.
3. Pre-existing gap this workload makes visible: nothing ever clears the embedding cache on `flush_cache`, so it can serve stale embeddings after a weight update. Separate-PR material, mentioning it here only because kept-rows work is adjacent.

This key is content identity (`item.hash`, or combined hash + offsets), not request identity — two session requests sharing one item object carry the same key. Correctness comes from the rows being content-determined plus the `next_token` guard, not from per-request isolation. Reword this comment (and the PR body's "tag the kept output with the request it belongs to") so the next reader doesn't assume an isolation that isn't there.

detail.body:
Fixes repeated video encoding in chunked prefill. A long video was run through the vision encoder once per chunk, so two or three times per request. Now it is encoded once.

## Motivation

When a prompt is longer than `chunked_prefill_size`, prefill runs in chunks. Each chunk looks for the encoder output in the embedding cache. If it is not there, the chunk runs the encoder again on the whole video, not only on the part it needs.

For a long video it is usually not there:

- The cache is 100 MiB by default. The encoder output of a long video is bigger than that, so it is never stored.
- Qwen3-VL on a Hopper GPU with 60 GiB or more runs with the cache off.
- An entry can be evicted between two chunks of the same request.

So a request with 3 chunks runs the encoder 3 times. A large image or an audio clip that is cut by a chunk boundary has the same problem.

I found this while profiling Qwen3-VL video requests: the vision encoder ran twice for one 16.5 s clip.

## Reproduction

Environment:

- GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB (`chunked_prefill_size` is 8192)
- Base: upstream `58cb1a2be6ab` for the first table (first version of this PR); upstream `abf92826ee` for the EVS table and the checks of this revision
- Server: default arguments. Qwen3.5-27B and the EVS model also get `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`, so the language-model prefill runs eagerly for every model.
- Input: synthetic 1280x720 clips, one video per request, streamed chat completions, 16 output tokens
- A forward hook on the vision encoder (on `mlp1` for the EVS model) counts how many times it runs per request.

| Model | Clip | Video tokens | Encoder output | Prefill chunks | Encoder runs before | Encoder runs after |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct` | 16.5 s | 9,216 | 288 MiB | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B` | 33.5 s | 11,550 | 113 MiB | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct` | 33.5 s | 23,760 | 162 MiB | 3 | 3 | 1 |
| `zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking` | 16.5 s | 20,332 | 159 MiB | 3 | 3 | 1 |

A shorter clip whose output fits the cache is encoded once on the base as well. For example the 16.5 s clip on Qwen3.5-27B has 9,216 tokens and 90 MiB of output, uses 2 chunks, and runs the encoder once.

EVS model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-BF16` with `video_pruning_rate` 0.7 (from its config), a 66 s clip (128 frames), one request at a time. At 0.7 the clip keeps 9,830 rows, 96 MiB, which fits the default 100 MiB cache, so these runs set `SGLANG_VLM_CACHE_SIZE_MB=0` to show the repeated encoding:

| Chunk size | Video tokens | Prefill chunks | Encoder runs before | Encoder runs after | Median TTFT before | Median TTFT after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 (default) | 9,830 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 5,875 ms | 5,411 ms |
| 2048 | 9,830 | 6 | 6 | 1 | 7,654 ms | 5,389 ms |

The TTFT values of this table come from one launch of 4 requests per tree. With the default cache both trees run the encoder once, and the change keeps the cache's own tensor instead of a copy. The server logs show EVS enabled at 0.7 and no warning or error.

A long video also emptied the cache for other requests: `MultiModalStaticCache.set()` evicted every entry before finding that the new one can never fit. `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct`, default 100 MiB cache, one request at a time, `--disable-radix-cache` (otherwise the repeated prompt would reuse its KV and never look at the cache). A 16.5 s clip (11,520 tokens, 79 MiB of encoder output, fits) is sent again after each of 8 different 33.5 s clips (23,760 tokens, 162 MiB, does not fit); 2 launches per tree, on `abf92826ee`:

| Tree | Encoder runs of the repeated 16.5 s clip | Its median TTFT | Median TTFT of the 33.5 s clips |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| this PR without the `set()` check | 16 of 16 requests | 1,098 ms | 2,422 ms |
| this PR | 0 of 16 | 833 ms | 2,420 ms |

## Modifications

- When the first chunk runs the encoder, keep the part of its output that later chunks still need, in a table in `mm_schedule` (`_prefill_rows`). The key is the item's hash and its positions in the prompt.
- Read the kept rows in later chunks before looking at the cache. In `_get_chunked_embedding_full` the cache is asked only when nothing is kept, so later chunks no longer touch its LRU order.
- Drop the part already read, so only the unread part stays in memory.
- Remove an entry after the item's last chunk. The scheduler also empties the table whenever no request is between two prefill chunks: at the start of `get_new_batch_prefill`, in the dLLM branch of `get_next_batch_to_run` while no context prefill is part-way (`DllmManager.any_context_in_progress()`), when a dLLM request is aborted, and in `pause_generation`, `flush_cache` and `release_memory_occupation`.
- Add `MultiModalStaticCache.peek()`, which reads an entry without changing the LRU order.
- `MultiModalStaticCache.set()` refuses an entry larger than the whole cache before evicting anything, so a long video no longer empties the cache for every other request. #42062 makes the same change.
- Check that the kept rows cover the chunk before slicing them.
- Cover the three chunked paths: `_get_chunked_embedding_full`, `_batch_encode_per_image_misses` and `_get_chunked_embedding_by_item`.
- Add unit tests for the three paths, EVS, a cache entry evicted between two chunks, an encoder that reuses its output buffer, a restarted prefill, items shared by session requests, the same image twice in one prompt, every place the scheduler empties the table, and an entry larger than the cache.

No new flag or config. A request that fits in one chunk takes the same path as before. `schedule_batch.py` is not changed, and nothing is stored in `model_specific_data`.

What is kept is a copy of the unread part, not the encoder output itself. The output can be a slice of a larger batch tensor, and keeping the slice would keep the whole batch alive. The copy is made again only after half of it has been read, so a video with many chunks is not copied once per chunk. If the cache holds the same tensor, it is kept by reference and nothing is copied; when `set()` stored a clone of the output, the clone is read and kept instead.

Requests with the same items at the same positions share an entry (session requests, identical prompts). That is safe because the rows depend only on the content, and a request reads an entry only from the position where its unread rows begin. The positions are part of the key because the same image twice in one prompt has the same hash; with the hash alone, the second copy would read rows of the first.

Where the table is emptied: `get_new_batch_prefill` is reached by every prefill loop after an abort, a disagg bootstrap failure or an optimistic yield has dropped the chunked request, and before a new request becomes the chunked one. Outside dLLM only the chunked request keeps rows into the next step, so the table holds the items of one request.

Making the cache bigger with `SGLANG_VLM_CACHE_SIZE_MB` does not fix this. The cache is shared and evicts the least recently used entry, so a request can still lose its entry between two chunks.

A precomputed embedding that is too short now fails at the new check instead of later in `_adjust_embedding_length`.

Not changed here: models that run the encoder inside their own `forward` (the legacy LLaVA family) have the same problem and need a separate change.

@JustinTong0323 Thanks a lot for the detailed review! I pushed the changes and replied to each comment above.

For the other three points:
- `set()` with an oversize entry: added the size check in e5830d1b59, so an entry that can't fit no longer empties the whole cache. I also checked it on a GPU with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and the default cache: a short clip sent again after long ones was re-encoded every time before (16 of 16) and never after (0 of 16), and its TTFT went from 1,098 to 833 ms.
- EVS: I ran Nemotron Nano 12B v2 VL on an H100. Its pruned output fits in the default cache, so I turned the cache off to reproduce the problem. The encoder ran once per chunk before (2 or 6 times, depending on chunk size) and once after, with identical outputs. Numbers are in the description.
- `flush_cache`: I'll open a separate PR for it.
